expectations.text: States that instructions to a model are not enforcement, regardless of wording or emphasis
expectations.evidence: Instructions to an agent are rung zero (training), and training degrades. A line in CLAUDE.md saying 'never do X' is not a device; it is a request the agent will eventually ignore as context length grows or subagents are spawned.

expectations.text: Redirects away from rewording CLAUDE.md as the primary fix
expectations.evidence: To actually stop these behaviors, you must replace the instructions with devices that block the actions before they execute.

expectations.text: Recommends permission deny rules in settings.json with concrete syntax
expectations.evidence: Provides explicit syntax with Edit, Write, and Bash deny patterns in a settings.json example block.

expectations.text: Recommends a PreToolUse hook for cases that need logic rather than a pattern match
expectations.evidence: your force push rule requires a PreToolUse hook script that can inspect the command with a regex to reliably catch the flag anywhere in the string

expectations.text: Explains that the deny message should say what to do instead, not merely refuse
expectations.evidence: The message must name what was blocked, why, and what to do instead. Example: Force-push can destroy commits. Use --force-with-lease if you must rewrite, or ask the user to run it.

expectations.text: Recommends verifying the device actually fires rather than assuming it works
expectations.evidence: Once installed, you must verify the devices. Ask the agent to edit a file in ./src/generated/ and separately ask it to run git push origin main -f. Confirm that both are blocked.

expectations.text: Recommends committing the rules so they apply to the whole team, not just one machine
expectations.evidence: Put these rules in .claude/settings.json and commit it to the repository. This ensures it applies to every agent session. A rule in settings.local.json only protects one machine.

expectations.text: Explains why repetition and capitals do not make an instruction reliable
expectations.evidence: Instructions to an agent are rung zero (training), and training degrades. A request the agent will eventually ignore as context length grows or subagents are spawned.
